diagnoses.rootCause: Three independent mechanisms upstream of any tie-break, each of which alone changes the retrieved set between two runs of one binary. (A) LLM-generated text feeds retrieval with no sampling control. HyDEService.swift:98 calls `session.respond(to: prompt)` with no `options:` argument, so Foundation Models uses its default stochastic sampling with no seed; the result becomes `textToEmbed` at RAGService.swift:9361, so the query embedding vector itself is different on every Deep Think / Maximum run (gated on at RAGQualityMode.swift:192). IterativeRetrievalService.swift:374 does the same for every refinement sub-query, and QueryRewriterService.swift:264 for ambiguous queries. LLMService.swift:750 is the only place a `GenerationOptions` is ever constructed, and its comment at :700 asserts "Every on-device generation passes through this line" — that is false for all 20 bare `respond(to:)` sites, so the harness's `--rag-validation-sampling greedy` override never reaches HyDE, the rewriter, or iterative refinement. (B) Per-process hash seeding decides which query-expansion terms survive a truncation. Swift seeds `Hasher` randomly per process — the repo states this itself at HybridSearchService.swift:176 — so `Set`/`Dictionary` iteration order differs between two launches. QueryEnhancementService.swift:914-919 sets `minCooccurrence` to the maximum count any term can reach, so the `.filter` leaves a set in which every element is tied, and `.sorted { $0.value > $1.value }.prefix(3)` then picks three arbitrary terms in hash order. Same shape at :988-994 (`Array(Set(...))` then a comparator with no final tiebreak, caller takes `.prefix(2)` at :932), :706 and :716 (dictionary iteration into a capped array), ContainerVocabularyService.swift:49-53, :194/:201/:210 and :226 (`Array(Set(expansions)).prefix(15)`), and GazetteerService.swift:228. All of it lands in `expandedQueries`, hard-capped at RAGService.swift:9180, then joined as the search query at :9555/:9623 and used to launch supplementary vector searches at :9670-9671 that append entirely new chunks to the candidate pool. This layer fires in Standard mode too, where HyDE and iterative retrieval are off. (C) Task-completion order feeds an unstable score-only sort inside the reranker, which every mode runs (RAGQualityMode.swift:199-201). RAGEngine.swift:1487 appends cross-encoder results in completion order, and :1501 and :1544 sort by score with no tiebreak; :1542's `max(0.01, ...)` clamp manufactures exact ties and :1516-1517 assigns a uniform 0.5 when the range collapses, so the `prefix(cappedTopK)` cut at :1546 keeps a different set. `HybridSearchService.stableTieBreakKey` cannot repair any of this: it is applied before reranking, and RAGEngine.swift:1028, HybridSearchService.swift:417 and :504 sort by score alone.

`vdb.search(embedding: suppEmbedding, topK: effectiveTopK)` over an expansion-derived embedding, whose new chunks are appended at :9675 — the randomized expansion changes the dense candidate pool, not only the lexical arm.

Comparing those four runs against the existing pair separates layer B from layers A and C at zero cost and tells you which fix to prioritize. run_quality_matrix.py:238 already records the variable, so the provenance lands in the report automatically.

The mechanisms are each individually certain from the source — a bare `respond(to:)` has no seed, an all-tied Dictionary `prefix(3)` is hash-ordered, a task group yields in completion order. What is NOT established is their relative contribution to the 21% figure. I did not run anything, so I cannot say fixing layer B alone moves reproducibility from 21% to any particular number, and I would not let anyone quote one. The `SWIFT_DETERMINISTIC_HASHING=1` re-run is the cheap way to attribute it and should happen before the code changes, or the fix will be credited to whichever layer was touched first. Unit tests can prove each function is now deterministic; they cannot prove end-to-end reproducibility, which needs two harness runs on the same frozen corpus.

Ruled out, with reasons: BNNSVectorDatabase.search is deterministic given the same `chunks` and `scores` — the unstable sorts at :549 and the heap at :558-591 produce the same output for the same input, and disk load order is stable. verdict.correction:
WHAT SURVIVED (verified line by line)

Layer A's factual core is CONFIRMED. `HyDEService.swift:98` is a bare `try await session.respond(to: prompt)` with no `options:`; same at `IterativeRetrievalService.swift:374` and `QueryRewriterService.swift:264`. `RAGService.swift:9361` is `let textToEmbed = hydeEmbeddingText ?? effectiveQuery`. `LLMService.swift:700` does carry the words "Every on-device generation passes through this line", and it is false: the benchmark override is read at `LLMService.swift:710-718` and `GenerationOptions` is constructed only at `LLMService.swift:750` (and its `#else` twin at :756), so the 19 bare `respond(to:...)` call sites repo-wide never see `benchmarkSamplingStrategy`. `--rag-validation-sampling` is written to that key at `DebugRAGValidationHarness.swift:135-146` and read nowhere else. That is a genuine, correctly diagnosed defect.

Layer C's mechanism is CONFIRMED and is the only one that reaches Standard mode. `RAGEngine.swift:1487` `for await result in group` / `:1489` `results.append(r)` genuinely produces a completion-ordered array; `:1501` `scoredChunks.sort { $0.score > $1.score }` and `:1544` are score-only; `:1542`'s `max(0.01, ...)` and `:1516-1517`'s uniform 0.5 exist; `:1546` is the `prefix(cappedTopK)` cut. `usesReRanking` is `true` for all modes (`RAGQualityMode.swift:199-201`), the asset exists (`OpenIntelligence/Resources/MLModels/ReRankerModel.mlpackage`), and `RAGEngine.swift:325` `await setupTask?.value` now guarantees the cross-encoder path is taken when the model loads.

The passing observation is CONFIRMED: `HybridSearchService.swift:954` computes `vectorResultsFiltered`, `:983-984` and `:1144` use it, but `:1091` fuses raw `vectorResults`. Real inconsistency, correctly flagged as out of scope.

WHAT FAILED

1. Layer B does not fire in Standard mode. The diagnosis states outright: "This layer fires in Standard mode too, where HyDE and iterative retrieval are off." `RAGQualityMode.swift:237-243`: `var usesQueryExpansion` returns `false` for `.standard`. `RAGService.swift:9151` gates the ENTIRE Step 1.5 block on it — the heuristic expansion at `:9171`, container vocabulary at `:9185-9189`, gazetteer at `:9206`. In Standard mode `expandedQueries` stays empty and `queryEnhancer.expandQuery` is never called from this path. The only ungated call is `RAGService.swift:18013` inside `executeFullRetrievalPipeline` (function at `:17919`), whose only callers are `AgenticOrchestrator.swift` (:996, :1755, :2086, :2324, :2436, :6161, :7412), and the orchestrator runs only in deepThink/maximum (`RAGQualityMode.swift:148-150`). Layer B is a Deep Think/Maximum defect only.

2. The anchoring evidence is Standard mode, so layers A and B cannot explain it. The 2026-08-16 divergence this row rests on (keyword hit rate 90 vs 91 percent, 77 chunks filtered vs none, 30 vs 14 MMR selections, 190 vs 350 character answers) was measured on `qasper_external_v1` in **standard** mode, per the commit body of `d3226de` and the project memory note. Standard has `usesHyDE=false` (`RAGQualityMode.swift:189-196`), `usesQueryRewriting=false` (:112-118), `usesIterativeRetrieval=false` (:121-128), `usesQueryExpansion=false` (:237-243). Of the three claimed mechanisms, only C is even in the circuit.

3. An already-landed competing fix is omitted. `RAGEngine.swift:50-62` documents a reranker model-load race that produced exactly this divergence — "Two runs of one build over byte-identical documents produced `Re-ranking complete. Top score: 1.2705` in one and `AI Re-ranking: raw -11.52 -> 5.61, normalized 0.10 -> 0.90` in the other. That is the upstream cause of the divergence recorded as Blocker 1." It was fixed in `24d3b54` ("stop a startup race choosing the ranking algorithm"), which lands AFTER `d3226de`. Whatever residual nondeterminism exists must be re-measured on current HEAD before it is attributed to A/B/C.

4. The repo's own leading hypothesis is neither addressed nor ruled out: float nondeterminism in embedding or BNNS vector search, amplified by the hard `0.28` floor at `RetrievalPolicyService.swift:107-108`. The candidate-set membership difference the keyword hit rate measured (`HybridSearchService.swift:365-366`, computed pre-rerank inside `applyKeywordMatchBoost` at :350) is upstream of the reranker entirely, so layer C cannot produce it either. The stated next measurement — embed one chunk twice and compare bit for bit — costs less than any part of this fix plan and is missing from it.

5. "Sorted by score with no tiebreak" is misdiagnosed as a source. Swift's `sorted(by:)` is unstable but fully deterministic: the same input array yields the same output every run. `HybridSearchService.swift:417` and `:504`, `RAGEngine.swift:397` (the plan says 398) and `:1028` all receive deterministically ordered inputs, so they propagate variance, they do not create it. Only `RAGEngine.swift:1501` has a genuinely nondeterministic input. Adding tiebreaks there is still worth doing as defense in depth, but presenting four extra sites as independent causes inflates the diagnosis.

6. Layer C's reach is asserted, not shown. Completion order changes the output only where the sort key ties exactly. Min/max normalization at `:1512-1514` is order-independent; the uniform-0.5 branch needs the whole batch range under 0.0001; the `max(0.01, ...)` clamp ties only chunks already driven to the floor by TOC/question-bank penalties, i.e. the bottom of the list, far from the `prefix(cappedTopK)` cut. "Alone changes the retrieved set between two runs" needs a demonstration.

7. The `minCooccurrence` reasoning is wrong for queries with 3+ substantive terms. `relatedTerms[coTerm, default: 0] += 1` at `QueryEnhancementService.swift:904` increments once per substantive query term, so the maximum reachable count is `substantiveTerms.count`, not 2. `:914`'s `substantiveTerms.count >= 2 ? 2 : 1` equals that maximum only at exactly 1 or 2 terms. For a four-term query, counts of 2, 3 and 4 all survive `:916` and the sort is informative. Ties remain common enough that `prefix(3)` at `:918` can land mid-tie, so the mechanism holds, but "a set in which every element is tied" is false in general.

8. `RAGService.swift:9180` is the wrong line for the mechanism. The append loop at `:9171-9176` already `break`s at `qualityModeMaxQueryExpansions`, so the `if count > max` at `:9179` fires only when the planner's own `searchQueries` (`:9167`) exceeded the cap. And the corpus nondeterminism needs no cap: `expandFromCorpus` emits one string at `:923` whose CONTENTS are the randomized three terms. Right conclusion, wrong line, wrong reason.

9. Minor citation drift: 19 bare `respond(to:)` call sites, not 20 (one grep hit at `FoundationModelStructuredGenerator.swift:107` is a comment, and several are `respond(to:generating:)`). `RAGEngine.swift:398` is 397. `GazetteerService.swift:228` is real but lives at `OpenIntelligence/Services/Document/Extraction/GazetteerService.swift`, and `vocabulary` is `[String: Set<String>]` (`:28`), so the mechanism there is right.

10. Unverified premise under layer A: that Apple's `respond(to:)` with no `options:` samples stochastically with an unseeded draw. Nothing in this repo establishes Foundation Models' default sampling mode. The comment at `LLMService.swift:679-681` establishes only that a seed matters for the random modes. Verify against developer.apple.com before justifying the change as a determinism fix.

FIX-PLAN REVIEW

Keep, and do first: the free attribution experiment. But re-baseline it on current HEAD (post-`24d3b54`), and note that the `SWIFT_DETERMINISTIC_HASHING=1` arm can only move Deep Think/Maximum — in Standard there is nothing hash-seeded in the expansion path to control, which is itself the cleanest way to confirm point 1 above. Add the bit-for-bit embedding comparison to the same batch; it is the cheapest discriminator between "ordering" and "floats".

Layer A fix is sound in shape (shared helper reading the same UserDefaults keys, no hardcoded `.greedy`, no shipped-behavior change). Two cautions: a new type placed under `OpenIntelligence/Services/` joins the OpenIntelligenceEngine framework target, which is how this repo has previously produced an app build that succeeds and a test build that fails with a scope error — place it deliberately. And do not reach for `FoundationModelSessionFactory.swift` or `FoundationModelRoutePolicy.swift` to host it; both are hard-boundary.

Layer C fix is safe. `input.chunkIndex` is `idx` from `chunks.enumerated()` at `RAGEngine.swift:1385/1412` and is unique, so a pre-sized indexed write, or sorting `scored` by index before `:1501`, breaks no caller; the function's return type is unchanged.

The regression guard as written does not work. Calling a pure function twice in one process cannot catch hash-seed nondeterminism, because the seed is constant within a process. And an exact-expected-list assertion would pass or fail per test-process launch rather than deterministically, so it would land as a flaky test. The honest guard is to make each comparator a total order and unit-test the comparator directly on constructed ties, plus a harness-level check that two runs with different `SWIFT_DETERMINISTIC_HASHING` settings agree.

diagnoses.rootCause:
`extractTextWithSpatialOrdering` builds the NSRange it hands to `page.selection(for:)` from a hand-maintained counter that under-counts the true offset in two independent ways, so every word after the first whitespace run is measured against the geometry of some *other* word earlier on the page.

Error 1 — collapsed separator runs. Line 7684 tokenizes with `pageString.split(whereSeparator:)`. `Collection.split` defaults `omittingEmptySubsequences: true`, so a run of N consecutive whitespace/newline characters yields no empty subsequences and is invisible to the loop. Line 7721 then advances the cursor by exactly `+1` "for separator". For every run longer than one character — a double space, an indent, a space-then-newline, a CRLF, a tab — the cursor falls behind by N-1. Leading whitespace on the page is dropped entirely by `split`, so the very first word is already misaligned when `page.string` starts with a space or newline.

Error 2 — wrong unit of measure. `wordString.count` at both 7691 (length) and 7721 (advance) is `String.count`, which counts extended grapheme clusters. `NSRange` addresses `page.string` in UTF-16 code units, because PDFKit's `selection(for:)` operates on the NSString backing. Every surrogate pair, every combining sequence, and every CRLF (one Character, two UTF-16 units) under-counts again.

Both errors are one-directional under-counts, so `wordIndex` is always ≤ the word's true UTF-16 location and the lag grows monotonically down the page. It therefore never runs past the end of the string and `selection(for:)` keeps returning a valid, non-nil selection — for the wrong text. Line 7694 takes `bounds` from that wrong text. From there every spatial decision is made on coordinates that do not describe the word being placed: the new-line test at 7698, the `midX` pushed into `lineXPositions` at 7717, `detectColumnBoundaries` at 7741, and the column assignment at 7758. Lines 7715 appends the *correct* word text, so the output contains all the right words carrying entirely fictional positions.

Why two-column PDFs specifically, and why they land on the raw path: the inter-column gutter and line padding are exactly what makes PDFKit's `page.string` full of multi-character whitespace runs, so a two-column page accumulates lag faster than any other layout. Once the lag is large, the lagging cursor only traverses a small prefix of the page while the loop walks every word, so the sampled `midY` values stay clustered within a few early lines, `isNewLine` at 7698 rarely fires, and `spatialLines` stays small. `guard spatialLines.count > 3 else { return nil }` at 7736 then returns nil, and both callers substitute the raw string: `layoutText = extractTextWithSpatialOrdering(from: page) ?? text` at 4207, and the untaken `if let` at 3472 leaving `effectiveString = pageString` from 3470. That raw string is the across-the-columns read the row describes. At moderate lag the function instead returns a confidently scrambled ordering that is still labelled `spatial-ordering` at 3575.

The discard is silent at every step, which is the signature failure class here. The `if let` at 7691 has no `else`: a word whose selection is nil or whose `selectionsByLine()` is empty is dropped from the line with no counter and no log. The nil return at 7736 logs nothing. The only log in the function, 7750, reports the *number of columns detected* — a number that reads perfectly healthy no matter how wrong the coordinates are. Downstream, 3566 computes `isSpatial` as `pageText != pageData.pageString`, so a scrambled result is reported as a successful spatial extraction with an unchanged character count, because the words really are all still present.

evidence.why: `pageString.split(whereSeparator: { $0.isWhitespace || $0.isNewline })` — `omittingEmptySubsequences` defaults to true, so runs of whitespace collapse to nothing and the loop cannot see how many separator characters it skipped. This is the fact that makes the `+1` on 7721 unrecoverable from inside the loop.

`wordIndex += wordString.count + 1 // +1 for separator` — hardcodes exactly one separator character per gap. Any double space, indent, tab, or CRLF makes the cursor lag by N-1, and the lag is cumulative and never corrected.

`page.selection(for: NSRange(location: wordIndex, length: wordString.count))` — NSRange is UTF-16 offsets into PDFKit's NSString-backed page string, but both `wordIndex` and `wordString.count` are grapheme-cluster counts. This is the exact line where the two number spaces are conflated.

`let bounds = firstChar.bounds(for: page)` — the geometry consumed for the rest of the function comes from whatever the drifted range selected, not from `wordString`. Everything after this point is computed on coordinates belonging to different text.

`currentLineText += (currentLineText.isEmpty ? "" : " ") + wordString` — the correct word text is appended while 7716/7717 record the wrong Y and X. This is why the output keeps a plausible character count and every log reads healthy: the words are all present, only their positions are fabricated.

`guard spatialLines.count > 3 else { return nil }` — the silent early return. Heavy lag suppresses `isNewLine` firings, `spatialLines` stays small, and the function bails to nil without logging anything.

Writing a ~150-line Python decoder against the real `.numbers` above, this chain works end to end: ZIP entry (stored) → IWA de-chunk (4-byte header: 0x00 then 3-byte LE chunk length; verified `00 cc 35 00` on `Index/Document.iwa` = 13772 bytes, file is 13776) → standard Snappy RAW BLOCK (varint uncompressed length then literal/copy tags; no stream identifier, no CRC — Apple deviates from the Snappy framing spec but not the block format) → TSP archive envelope (varint length, `ArchiveInfo{ id:1, repeated MessageInfo:2{ type:1, length:3 } }`, then payloads) → message type 2001 = `TSWP.StorageArchive`, field 3 = text. Route 1 (the no-op that reports success). At RAGService.swift:7080-7083 the exclusion set `activeUrls` is built from **every** element of `ingestionItems` with no stage filter at all — not just non-terminal ones, as the row assumed. Line 7086 then drops any document whose `fileURL` appears there. The comment at :7087 says the guard exists to prevent duplicate extraction pipelines for items "already queued or paused"; terminal items are finished work and must not veto anything.

2. Stop returning success for a vetoed rebuild. Split the empty case at :7091-7103:

   - `!containerDocuments.isEmpty && documentsToRebuild.isEmpty` → throw a new `RAGServiceError.rebuildBlockedByQueue(blocked: Int)` case (enum at :17824) whose message names the blocking items.
   Then fix the three callers:

   - `kickPendingReembedIfNeeded` (:4849): same — re-insert the banner instead of only logging.
   - `ContainerSettingsSheet.startReembedding` (:834): surface `reembedError` instead of dismissing at :832.

A crash, a suppressed kick, or a cancel then leaves a visible banner instead of an invisible empty store.

diagnoses.riskIfWrong:
The veto at :7086 is load-bearing: it stops a rebuild from re-entering the extraction pipeline for a document an import is currently working on, and RAGService has a documented re-entrancy loop (comment at :7774-7778, addDocument → refreshIntelligence → scheduleSelfTuningRebuild). Filter it to non-terminal items rather than deleting it; deleting it risks duplicate documents and duplicate chunks, and the duplicate-detection path is already known to be weak (SampleDocumentManager.swift:280-295 documents managed-path uniquifying defeating the existing duplicate check, which produced nine copies of three samples).

Second risk: throwing on the blocked case turns a currently-silent path into a user-visible error. If the blocked case is common in normal use (it will be, until the reaper in step 4 lands, because terminal items linger), users will see rebuild failures where they previously saw nothing. Ship steps 1, 2 and 4 together, not step 2 alone.

Third: only the pure selection function is provable off-device. That the rebuild then actually refills the store, that the banner reappears, and that route 2 no longer strands an emptied store are all device claims. Retrieval here is roughly 21% reproducible run to run and the agentic path has no coverage, so do not treat a green suite as evidence the cycle is fixed — this needs a device trace showing (a) a self-heal that logs blocked instead of "completed successfully", and (b) a library whose vector count goes from 0 to non-zero.

Fourth: adding `createdAt` to IngestionItem changes the shape of a file written through WorkspaceSyncService coordinated writes and read by other devices in a shared workspace. Prefer the `events.last?.timestamp` route, which needs no schema change; if the field is added, it must be optional with decodeIfPresent so older queue files and older app versions on other devices still decode.

diagnoses.rootCause: Chunk boundaries are selected on CHARACTER offsets, then "snapped" to sentence boundaries by two helpers that can silently return the edge of their own search window instead of a real linguistic boundary. `findNearestSentenceEnd` (SemanticChunker.swift:1369) and `findNearestSentenceStart` (:1410) each build a substring by slicing the document at arbitrary character offsets (`index ± distance`), run `NLTokenizer(unit: .sentence)` over that fragment, and accept a token's upperBound/lowerBound as a boundary. Given a fragment that begins and ends mid-sentence, NLTokenizer emits one token spanning the whole fragment, so the helper returns the ARTIFICIAL SLICE EDGE — a pure character offset — and reports success. Neither helper validates that the index it returns is preceded by sentence-terminating punctuation or even sits at a whitespace boundary, and neither logs when it degrades. Two cuts result. (1) Chunk START: `advancePosition` (:1859) computes a correct word-aligned overlap start at :1872, then hands it to `findNearestSentenceStart(..., within: 30)` at :1875 and returns whatever comes back if it lies inside the chunk (:1877-1879). I transcribed the shipped code verbatim and ran it: the helper returned the -30-character window edge in 33 of 40 probes on ordinary technical prose, and 3 of 8 resulting chunk starts landed mid-word ("...reinsert it fully, and withdraw it again to obta | in an accurate reading of the current level"). Every chunk after the first goes through this path. (2) Chunk END: the fallback in `findOptimalChunkRange` (:1291-1332) — the path that runs whenever no section, table end, or transition phrase falls in range, i.e. most ordinary prose — never touches word or token positions. It splits on the literal ASCII space (:1293), reconstructs a character length assuming exactly one space between every pair of words (:1316), offsets into the string by that number (:1323), then calls `findNearestSentenceEnd(..., within: 100)` (:1330). Inside any sentence longer than ~200 characters the helper returns `index + 100`: 8 of 12 probes landed mid-word ("...cleaning solution is appl | ied to any surface..."). The :1316 arithmetic also drifts independently — `omittingEmptySubsequences: true` discards runs of spaces, so on space-padded PDF-column text the computed length was 1969 against a true span of 2099, a 130-character undershoot over 260 words, landing mid-word before the snap even runs. The distinction that matters: the PREFERRED boundaries are all correctly aligned (section starts :1246, table ends :1262, transition phrases :1276, embedding boundaries :1198). Only the fallback is character arithmetic, and its snap step cannot fail loudly. The one genuinely word-aligned operation in the file is the hard-limit truncation at :440-464, which uses real NLTokenizer word ranges — but it only trims the tail of oversized chunks. Nothing trims or repairs chunk text afterward: `String(text[chunkRange])` at :437 is stored verbatim, with no `trimmingCharacters` anywhere in the assembly path. This is invisible to the guard built to catch exactly this: `verifyContentCoverage` (DocumentProcessor.swift:6633) unions unique words across all chunks, and the intact word still exists in the preceding chunk's overlap region, so it logs "✅ Content coverage: 100.0% words" while boundaries are shredding words.

advancePosition hands the word-aligned overlap start to findNearestSentenceStart(within: 30) and, at :1878, returns whatever it gets if it lies inside the chunk. Verified by running the transcribed code: the helper returned the window edge in 33/40 probes, and 3/8 chunk starts landed mid-word ('to obta | in an accurate reading').

diagnoses.fixSketch: Five changes, all in SemanticChunker.swift. (2) Make both snap helpers refuse to return their own window edge: in findNearestSentenceEnd (:1369) and findNearestSentenceStart (:1410), reject any candidate whose mapped index equals searchStart/searchEnd, and additionally require a real terminator (`.!?` or newline) adjacent to the candidate. Return nil when no genuine boundary exists in range, and log at debug when that happens so the degradation stops being silent. (3) Make every caller handle nil by falling back to a WORD boundary rather than a raw character offset: route :1323, :1331 and the final `return start..<targetIndex` at :1363 through snapToWordBoundary. (4) Replace the fallback's character arithmetic at :1293-1327 with NLTokenizer word-range enumeration from `start` — take the `config.targetSize`-th token's upperBound directly. This deletes the :1316 drift entirely and makes the pre-snap index already word-aligned, so a failed sentence snap degrades to "cuts at a word" instead of "cuts mid-word". (5) In advancePosition (:1859), stop re-finding the overlap by substring search: enumerate word ranges over `text[start..<chunkEnd]` and take the `overlap`-th-from-last range's lowerBound directly, then snap sentence-ward only if a real boundary is found. Do NOT also rewrite chunkTextWithBoundaries' missing hard limit in this change — it is unreachable in the shipping app and folding it in would make the diff untestable; file it separately. verdict.correction:
Six corrections. Act on the first two before implementing.

(1) SCOPE ERROR — evidence items 4 and 6 (the :1316 multi-space drift and the silent zero-overlap at :1872) are DEAD for PDFs, scans and images, this app's dominant document types. OCRConfiguration.normalizeExtractedText step 6 (OCRConfiguration.swift:524-531) collapses [^\S\n]{2,} to a single space, and DocumentProcessor.normalizationProfile(for:) (:8240-8252) routes everything outside the authored list to .extractedDocument, so PDF/image/scan text reaches the chunker with no runs of spaces. Those two failures are live only for .authoredText: text, markdown, rtf, code, csv, Word/Excel/PowerPoint/Pages/Numbers/Keynote, and audio/video transcripts. That is still a wide surface and the mechanism is real — on double-spaced text all 3 of my simulated transitions hit the nil range(of:) match, returned chunkEnd, and produced ZERO overlap with no log line — but the diagnosis presents it as a general pipeline property. A reviewer testing with a PDF will fail to reproduce it and may discard the whole row.

(2) HOLE IN THE FIX PLAN — buildParentContent (:1450-1454) has the identical defect and is not covered. It calls findNearestSentenceStart(..., within: 120) ?? lower and findNearestSentenceEnd(..., within: 120) ?? upper. Today those return the ±120 window edge; after fix step (2) makes the helpers return nil, the ?? falls back to lower/upper, which are raw range.lowerBound-250 and upperBound+250 character offsets — equally mid-word. Fix step (3) enumerates callers ":1323, :1331 and :1363" and omits :1453-1454. parentContent is what reaches the model as context (DocumentProcessor:935 and :5146 pass it as ProcessedChunk.parentText), so leaving it uncovered means the fix cleans the indexed chunk and not the text the model reads. Route :1453 and :1454 through snapToWordBoundary too.

(3) Fix step (4) is not size-neutral, and the plan should say so. NLTokenizer(.word) emits ~4% more tokens than split(separator: " ") and drops punctuation entirely (measured: 584 vs 561 on technical prose), so taking the 260th token's upperBound yields a chunk about 3.6% shorter in characters (1385 vs 1437 chars). Every boundary in every library shifts. It is still the right change — it makes the cut agree with tokenWordCount (:91), which the hard limit and every log line already use — but it invalidates any retrieval baseline recorded before it, so sequence it against the v5.0 embedding measurement work rather than landing it mid-run.

(4) One mechanism, not two, for the chunk END. The diagnosis says the :1316 arithmetic lands mid-word "before the snap even runs". On single-spaced text that arithmetic is exact: sum of token lengths plus (N-1) single separators puts targetIndex precisely at the end of the Nth token, i.e. word-aligned. The mid-word end comes only from the +100 snap edge inside sentences longer than ~200 chars. And the measured drift magnitude is far smaller than claimed: 14 chars over 260 tokens on double-spaced prose, not 130 over 260 words. Drop the 1969/2099 figure.

(5) Severity is overstated by the "silent truncation" framing. No content is lost in the normal case: the overlap region duplicates the preceding chunk, so the shredded word survives whole in chunk N while chunk N+1 opens with its tail. The cost is a garbage leading token per chunk and an ugly boundary in cited snippets. The genuine loss case is narrow — authored text with multi-space runs, where the nil match zeroes the overlap and the seam word exists nowhere intact.

(6) None of the diagnosis's probe counts reproduce as written (33/40, 3/8, 8/12, 1969 vs 2099). My independent runs give 43/59, 2/3, 8/22 and drift 14. The mechanism reproduces; the numbers do not. Whatever lands in Docs/INGESTION_PIPELINE.md or the CHANGELOG must come from a re-run on this machine, not from the diagnosis text. Also drop "every chunk after the first goes through this path" as a claim about outcomes — every chunk goes through advancePosition, but the share that ends up mid-word was 66-73% on technical prose and depends on the sentence-length distribution of the library.

The row bundles two items with opposite status, and the honest finding is that the query-side half is already done and the schema half is unavoidable.

(1) BM25 COLUMN WEIGHTING — NO DEFECT REMAINS. The misalignment this row describes was fixed 2026-08-06 (Docs/ROADMAP.md:49). All four `bm25(chunks, ...)` sites (SQLiteFullTextService.swift:1458, 1461, 1468, 1471) now pass exactly 9 weights `0,0,0,0,0,10.0,5.0,0,1.0` for the 9 declared columns of `chunks` (:242-255), correctly aligned to section_title=10, section_path=5, content=1. The other two FTS5 tables each have exactly ONE indexed column — `documents` (:191-197, only `content`) and `document_pages` (:321-329, only `content`) — so `bm25(documents)` at :1568/:1577/:1639/:1648/:1791 and `bm25(document_pages)` at :518/:522 are correct as written and have nothing to weight. There is no shippable query-side weighting slice hiding here.

I actively ruled out three plausible silent defects rather than assuming them. (a) `columnsize=0` on `chunks` (:253) does NOT degrade bm25: reproduced in sqlite3 3.54 against a `columnsize=1` twin over 202 docs with deliberately divergent lengths and got bit-identical scores (-7.2239 short / -1.4590 long), so length normalization is intact. (b) The abs() at HybridSearchService.swift:1019 correctly handles both score families — native bm25 (negative) and the synthetic positive scores from the `searchStructuredChunks` fallback (:1541). (c) The `"a" "b"` juxtaposition emitted by `escapeFTS5Query` (:3263) really is an order-independent implicit AND, as its comment claims (verified: `"beta" "alpha"` and `"alpha" "beta"` both return only the row containing both).

One real constraint on any future weight tuning: RRF is purely RANK-based (RAGEngine.swift:1004, `keywordWeight / Float(k + rank + 1)`), so weight magnitudes never enter the fused score — they only reorder the lexical arm. Tuning 10/5/1 is therefore possible but unfalsifiable today, and note section_path structurally contains section_title as its last component ("Maint > Engine Oil"), so a heading term is effectively worth 15x, not 10x.

(2) TRIGRAM FOR IDENTIFIERS — GENUINELY ABSENT AND GENUINELY REQUIRED. Mechanism: `tokenize='porter unicode61'` (:252) splits on every non-alphanumeric and matches whole tokens only, so it cannot do infix. Measured in sqlite3 against the real schema: query "urlsession" MISSES indexed "NSURLSession"; query "90915" MISSES indexed "90915YZZD1". I tested the two cheaper alternatives and both fail. `tokenchars='-_.'` is strictly WORSE — it regressed two cases the current tokenizer wins ("AB 1234"→AB-1234, and "1000xm5"→WH-1000XM5) while fixing none. `prefix='2 3 4'` produced results identical to current on all 8 identifier cases, because prefix matching is anchored at token start and so can never reach an infix, and because the query builder never emits `*`. Trigram was the only configuration that recovered the infix cases. Critically, trigram is COMPLEMENTARY, not a replacement: it LOSES "AB 1234"→"AB-1234" which porter wins. That measurement validates the second-table-plus-RRF design in Docs/Engineering/RETRIEVAL_UPGRADE_PLAN_2026-08.md:75-92 and rules out swapping the tokenizer in place.

Two silent-truncation hazards specific to this change, both measured, both of the exact shape this repo keeps getting bitten by:
  H1 — THE NEW TABLE IS EMPTY FOR EVERY EXISTING LIBRARY. `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is additive and compiles clean, the trigram arm then returns 0 rows forever for anyone who already ingested, `[Hybrid] FTS5 found N chunks...` (HybridSearchService.swift:1078) keeps reading healthy, and a fresh-install dev test passes. Needs an explicit one-time backfill.
  H2 — TRIGRAM SILENTLY DROPS QUERY PHRASES UNDER 3 CHARACTERS. Measured: `"filter" "zz"` returns the same rows as `"filter"` alone (the constraint simply vanishes, no error), while `"filter" "zzz"` correctly returns empty; `"zz"` alone returns zero rows with no error. `escapeFTS5Query` admits terms at `count >= 2` (:3249, and :3285 in the Broad variant), so every 2-char term ("V6", "M8", "AC", "ID") is honored by the porter arm and silently ignored by the trigram arm.

Cost is materially higher than the plan assumes. Measured on 2000 synthetic prose chunks: base `chunks` DB 9.30 MB; content-only contentless trigram → 18.93 MB (+104%); 3-column self-content trigram → 28.14 MB (+202%). The plan's "roughly one extra index's worth of disk" understates this by 2-3x.

Structural constraints I verified so the plan does not go down dead ends: external-content FTS5 over the `chunks` virtual table FAILS ("no such table: main.chunks"), and so does a VIEW wrapping it — so `content='chunks'` + `'rebuild'` is off the table. A self-content trigram table works, and `INSERT INTO chunks_tri(rowid, ...) SELECT rowid, ... FROM chunks` backfills the whole index in one statement with no re-ingest, with the rowid join back to `chunks` resolving correctly. Contentless (`content=''`) cannot DELETE at all ("table does not support scanning") unless `contentless_delete=1`, and then only by rowid — which does not fit `deleteChunks(for:)` (:978) and `deleteChunksForContainer` (:996), both of which delete by document_id/container_id.

      section_title, content, tokenize='trigram')

diagnoses.rootCause:
F-03 is `Docs/AUDIT/ROADMAP_RECONCILIATION_2026-07-28.md:75` ("Dynamic candidate cutoff remains unfixed"), whose open roadmap item is `Docs/ROADMAP.md:74`. Both point at one line, which has drifted from `RAGEngine.swift:297` to `RAGEngine.swift:318`: `let adaptiveCeiling = min(chunks.count, max(100, min(250, topK * 5)))`, applied at :319 as `Array(chunks.prefix(adaptiveCeiling))`. It is NOT in HybridSearchService or RetrievalPolicyService; RetrievalPolicyService contains no candidate cutoff at all.

Two findings, and the first contradicts the roadmap.

(1) THE ROADMAP DESCRIBES A DEFECT THAT DOES NOT EXIST. It asks to stop "hardcoding a floor of 100 chunks" for small libraries. `max(100, ...)` can only make the pool LARGER, and `min(chunks.count, ...)` already bounds it, so a 60-chunk library gets 60, never 100. For `max(100, ...)` to be the binding term you need `topK*5 <= 100` (topK <= 20) AND `chunks.count > 100` simultaneously. Enumerating every reachable caller: the main path passes `topK: effectiveTopK * 3` (RAGService.swift:10022) where `effectiveTopK >= 15` always (:8786), so topK_arg >= 45; IterativeRetrievalService.swift:246 passes `min(allChunks.count, topK*2)`, which caps the arg at the pool size; RAGService.swift:18076 passes `topK*2` against a pool of at most `topK*2`; RAGService.swift:11476 uses `max(effectiveTopK*3, 10)`. The floor is unreachable as the binding term. Implementing the roadmap's stated fix would change zero behavior.

(2) THE REAL DEFECT IS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION: A CONSTANT 250 THAT FIGHTS THE CORPUS-SIZE LADDER. Because topK_arg >= 45 in every path, `min(250, topK*5)` saturates and the ceiling is effectively the constant 250. Meanwhile RAGService.swift:8783-8802 deliberately scales `topK` with corpus size up to 200 ("Massive corpus (15000+): topK = 150-250"), hybrid search is called at `effectiveTopK * 3` (:9626) and returns exactly that many (`HybridSearchService.swift:312` and `:1142`, `prefix(topK)`), then multi-vector supplementary search appends up to `2 * effectiveTopK` more (:9671-9675). Pool size is therefore up to `5 * effectiveTopK`, and 250 clips it whenever `effectiveTopK > 50`, i.e. from `totalStored >= 2500` (:8793). At 2,500-5,000 chunks up to 33% of the fused pool is discarded; at 20,000+ chunks (`effectiveTopK = 200`, pool up to 1,000) up to 75% is discarded. The app widens the net for large corpora and a constant one layer down clips it back.

The discard is worse than uniform. Supplementary multi-vector chunks are APPENDED to the tail (:9675) and the array is only re-sorted if `demotedCount > 0` (:9913-9914) or if `applyMetadataBoost` returns non-nil (:9977-9982). `prefix()` cuts from the tail. So in the common case where neither sort fires, the first chunks the ceiling destroys are exactly the ones "UNIVERSAL FIX 9" added to catch needles the primary embedding missed. Above ~5,000 chunks the hybrid arm alone fills the 250 (3 * 84 > 250), so every supplementary chunk is discarded, every time.

IT DOES NOT LOG WHAT IT DROPPED — this is textbook silent truncation:
- No log between :318 and the cross-encoder return at :330. The only count log is :342-346, which runs only on the heuristic-fallback path and prints `candidateChunks.count`, the POST-truncation number.
- RAGService.swift:9676 logs "+N new chunks from expansion" for supplementary chunks that are then discarded wholesale downstream. The log line reads healthy and is actively misleading.
- `auditCandidatesCount = chunksWithSources.count` (:9918) is the PRE-ceiling count, and it is what the user-facing audit view and the SDK report as "Candidates". It overstates what the reranker actually scored.
- The benchmark trace has no measurement point at the cutoff. `.candidates` is recorded by HybridSearchService (:336, :1148) as the reranker's INPUT; `.rerank` is recorded by RAGService (:10069) as its OUTPUT. The ceiling drop is folded into that interval, which falsifies the documented diagnostic at RetrievalTraceCollector.swift:85-86 ("a drop from `.candidates` to `.rerank` means the cross-encoder demoted the right chunk") — it can equally mean the ceiling cut the chunk before the cross-encoder ever scored it, and no artifact can tell them apart. `Docs/RETRIEVAL_PIPELINE.md:29-30,38` draws a `Cutoff` node with `Cutoff -.-> Trace`; that trace edge does not exist in code.

The doc comment at :312-317 does not describe the formula it sits above. "Small corpus (<200 chunks): use all chunks (no artificial ceiling)" and "Medium corpus: topK * 5 (50 candidates for topK=10)" are both false under the actual call parameters, where topK is never 10 and the floor always wins over topK*5.

HONESTY BOUND: this mechanism is established by static analysis, not observed in any recorded failure. It cannot fire on any corpus this project has evidence for. The benchmark fixture is one Sportage manual (`HybridSearchService.swift:305` records that corpus as 300 chunks) and the device traces on record are 181-420 chunks (CHANGELOG.md:213, :224, :258) — an order of magnitude below the >=2,500 trigger. Do not sell this as the cause of any observed retrieval miss.

diagnoses.fixSketch:
Four parts. Parts A and B are the fix; C and D are what stops it being another unverifiable tuning change.

A. CORRECT THE ROADMAP BEFORE TOUCHING CODE. `Docs/ROADMAP.md:74` states a defect that does not exist. Run the `oi-claim-audit` skill and rewrite the row from "remove the 100 floor for small libraries" to the actual finding: a constant 250 ceiling that does not scale with the corpus. Do not delete the old text — supersede it in place, per the evidence protocol, so the record shows the original claim was wrong. Same for the F-03 section of `Docs/AUDIT/ROADMAP_RECONCILIATION_2026-07-28.md:75-85`, whose "Small libraries still get a 100-chunk pool" is false.

B. REPLACE THE FORMULA WITH ONE THAT SCALES, AND EXTRACT IT SO IT CAN BE TESTED. Pull the arithmetic out of `rerank` into a pure, internal static function so a test can reach it without CoreML:

    static func crossEncoderCandidateCeiling(poolSize: Int, topK: Int, latencyBudget: Int) -> Int

Behavior it should have, stated as invariants rather than a magic number:
  - Never smaller than `topK`. Truncating below the number of results you are about to return is incoherent; today `topK_arg = effectiveTopK*3` can reach 600 while the ceiling is 250.
  - Scale with the requested pool, not with a constant: something like `min(poolSize, max(topK, latencyBudget))` where `latencyBudget` is derived from `AdaptivePipelineOptimizer` (which already publishes `maxRetrievalCandidates`, 10 to 250, thermal- and memory-aware) rather than hardcoded at the call site. That makes one policy own pool size instead of two policies fighting.
  - Drop `max(100, ...)` entirely. It is unreachable as the binding term and its only effect is to make the comment lie.

C. MAKE THE DISCARD SPEAK. This is the part the defect class demands, and it is worth more than the number change:
  - At `RAGEngine.swift:319`, when `adaptiveCeiling < chunks.count`, `Log.warning` with pool size, ceiling, how many were dropped, and how many of the dropped were supplementary-origin. Warn, not debug — `.info` is how the self-healing suppression hid for a release (CHANGELOG.md:213).
  - Add a `.ceiling` case to `RetrievalTraceCollector.Stage` between `.candidates` and `.rerank`, recorded from `RAGService` around the rerank call, and fix the now-false doc comment at `RetrievalTraceCollector.swift:85-86`. Without this, a recall drop at rerank remains unattributable, and the harness's whole claim is that any number can be recomputed by hand.
  - Change `auditCandidatesCount` (`RAGService.swift:9918`) to record what the reranker actually scored, or add a second field, so the audit UI stops overstating.
  - Sort `chunksWithSources` before the rerank call unconditionally, so the ceiling cuts the lowest-scoring chunks rather than whichever ones happened to be appended last. Today the tail order depends on whether `demotedCount > 0` fired, which is an unrelated condition.

D. DO NOT TUNE THE NUMBER YET. `HybridSearchService.swift:417` and `:504` sort by `similarityScore`, which after `RAGEngine.swift:1028` is raw cosine/BM25, not the RRF score. The fused ordering is destroyed before `prefix(topK)` runs, so "the top 250" does not mean "the top 250 by fusion". Raising 250 to 500 over a list that is not fused-ordered is noise, and it plausibly bears on the recorded finding that RRF scores worse than the lexical arm alone. File that as its own row and fix it before claiming any quality delta from this one.
diagnoses.riskIfWrong:
Verification splits into three tiers and only the first is provable today, which is the main risk of overclaiming here.

Tier 1, provable now, no device: the binding-term analysis is a closed-form enumeration over the reachable topK domain. `effectiveTopK >= 15` (RAGService.swift:8786) forces `topK_arg >= 45` at every one of the five rerank call sites, so `min(250, topK*5)` saturates and `max(100, ...)` never binds. A static count over the call sites settles it. This is what `verifiableBy: static_count` refers to.

Tier 2, provable after the refactor in fix part B: a unit test on the extracted pure ceiling function. It does not exist today — grep finds zero tests referencing `RAGEngine` anywhere in `OpenIntelligenceTests`, and `rerank` currently awaits `setupTask` and a CoreML model, so it is not directly unit-testable in its present shape.

Tier 3, NOT provable today: whether raising the ceiling recovers any actual needle. The 25-case benchmark runs against a ~300-chunk corpus (HybridSearchService.swift:305) and the device traces on record are 181-420 chunks (CHANGELOG.md:213, :224, :258). The ceiling first binds at ~2,500 chunks. Nothing in this repository can currently exercise the code path, so any claimed recall improvement would be fabricated. Combined with retrieval being only ~21% reproducible run to run, an A/B on this would be uninterpretable even with a big enough corpus.

Concrete risk of shipping the change: raising the ceiling directly raises cross-encoder cost, which is O(n) CoreML forward passes at 512 tokens each. Going from 250 to 600 on a 20,000-chunk library is 2.4x the rerank latency on exactly the largest, slowest libraries, on device, under whatever thermal state produced the small `maxRetrievalCandidates` in the first place. That is why fix part B routes the budget through `AdaptivePipelineOptimizer` rather than hardcoding a larger constant. Getting this wrong ships a thermal regression to the users with the biggest libraries, and the benchmark will show nothing either way.

Secondary risk: the trace-stage addition changes `RetrievalTraceCollector.Stage`, which `DebugRAGValidationHarness` reads and which the STAGE SOURCES/STAGE METRICS artifact format depends on. Adding a stage mid-pipeline shifts the columns of every future benchmark artifact and makes them non-comparable to the 25/25 run already recorded. Freeze inputs and note the format change in the artifact, or prior runs will silently look like they measured something else.

Six defects. None overturns the root cause; four weaken the argument, two weaken the fix.

1. MISATTRIBUTED CITATION WITH A FALSE INVARIANT (the only real error of fact). The diagnosis cites "RAGService.swift:8786 — effectiveTopK floor: max(15, min(totalStored, 20)). Guarantees topK_arg into rerank is >= 45." Line 8786 is the `case 0..<100` branch of `corpusSizeAdjustedTopK`, not effectiveTopK. effectiveTopK is defined at :8818 as `min(uncappedEffectiveTopK, adaptiveMaxTopK)`, where `adaptiveMaxTopK = adaptiveConfig.maxRetrievalCandidates` (:8814) bottoms out at 10 (AdaptivePipelineOptimizer.swift:251 `.minimal`, and :344 `min(10, adjusted.maxRetrievalCandidates)` for trivial complexity). So effectiveTopK can be 10 and topK_arg 30; "effectiveTopK >= 15 always" and "topK_arg >= 45" are both false.
   The conclusion survives for a stronger reason the diagnosis did not find: pool size and topK_arg are both proportional to effectiveTopK. Pool <= 5*effectiveTopK, while topK_arg*5 = 15*effectiveTopK = three times the maximum pool. The floor binds only if chunks.count > 100 AND topK_arg*5 < 100, but chunks.count > 100 forces topK_arg*5 > 300. Contradiction at any effectiveTopK. Substitute this argument for the :8786 one; it needs no assumption about effectiveTopK's floor. (I checked the IterativeRetrieval path separately: iterative retrieval is disabled in .balanced/.efficient/.minimal and in the trivial branch, so wherever it runs adaptiveMaxTopK >= 40 and the floor is non-binding there too.)

2. INCOMPLETE ENUMERATION. "Enumerating every reachable caller" lists four; there are six. RAGService.swift:10127 (cascade rerank) and :10238 (keyword-retry rerank) are also `engine.rerank` call sites. Both pass `effectiveTopK * 3`, so the conclusion is unaffected, but the completeness claim as written is false and should be restated over six sites.

3. FINDING (2) OMITS A DEVICE-TIER GATE, overstating the affected population. Because effectiveTopK = min(corpus ladder, adaptiveMaxTopK), the 250 ceiling binds only when adaptiveMaxTopK >= 75. On a device where `maxRetrievalCandidates` is 40 (AdaptivePipelineOptimizer.swift:124), effectiveTopK <= 40, pool <= 200, and the ceiling never binds at any corpus size. The trigger is "corpus >= 2500 AND mid-or-high device tier", not corpus size alone. The percentages quoted (33% at 2.5-5k, 75% at 20k+) are arithmetically right but are best-case-tier figures.

4. PART B DOES NOT FIX THE HARM PART 2 IDENTIFIES. The proposed `min(poolSize, max(topK, latencyBudget))` takes `topK` = the rerank argument = effectiveTopK*3, with poolSize up to 5*effectiveTopK and latencyBudget = maxRetrievalCandidates >= effectiveTopK. Whenever 3*effectiveTopK > adaptiveMaxTopK — true in most of the regime this targets — the ceiling resolves to 3*effectiveTopK, which still cuts exactly the 2*effectiveTopK supplementary chunks appended at the tail. The formula satisfies its own "never smaller than topK" invariant while still discarding 100% of the multi-vector supplementary chunks in the large-corpus case the diagnosis calls the worst. Part C's unconditional pre-rerank sort changes which chunks die, not how many. Either state the intended invariant as "never smaller than the pool the pipeline deliberately assembled" (i.e. admit poolSize when latency allows), or drop the claim that this recovers the UNIVERSAL FIX 9 chunks.

5. PART C OMITS A REQUIRED CONSUMER UPDATE. `scripts/save_benchmark_summary.py:36` hardcodes `STAGE_ORDER = ["vector","lexical","fusion","boosted","candidates","rerank","final"]`. Adding a `.ceiling` stage without editing that line lands it at the end of the report, because :109 appends unrecognised stages after the known ones. Not a break (nothing switches exhaustively over `RetrievalTraceCollector.Stage`; `Stage.allCases` at DebugRAGValidationHarness.swift:402 and RAGEvalRunner.swift:199 pick up a new case automatically), but the plan should name it.

The test would pass identically if `extractTextFromAudioVideo` were deleted. The one unexplained cold-start stall documented at lines 220-228 is most plausibly the TCC alert appearing with nobody to tap it, not a pipeline hang.

The fixture reinforces this: `silentWAV()` writes a valid RIFF header over `Data(count: 32000)` — pure zeros (IngestionFixtureFactory.swift:244). No test in the repo has ever put a speech waveform through this path.

(2) WHAT THE GAP CONCEALED — a live silent fallback. `#if canImport(SpeechAnalyzer)` guards every iOS 26+ code path in SpeechAnalyzerService.swift (lines 17, 94, 141, 160). Therefore `canImport` is false in every build, `isSpeechAnalyzerAvailable` is a compile-time constant `false` (line 99), and `analyze()` always reaches `legacyTranscription` (line 148) → SFSpeechRecognizer. Every audio and video file the app has ever ingested went through the legacy recognizer while DocumentProcessor.swift:8490 logged "via SpeechAnalyzer". The dead branch would not compile against the real SDK even if reached: `SpeechAnalyzer(locale:)` (line 169) and `analyzer.results(for: url)` (line 179) do not exist. diagnoses.fixSketch:
Three tiers. Ship tier 1 and 2 regardless; tier 3 only if the simulator gates open.

TIER 1 — stop the existing test passing for the wrong reason (cheap, deterministic, runs today).
`IngestionProcessingOutcome.threw(String)` already carries the error description (IngestionFormatCoverageTests.swift:11, populated at 365) and it is currently discarded. Bind it and assert: the throw must be `audioTranscriptionEmpty` or an `audioTranscriptionFailed` whose reason mentions no speech. `authorizationDenied`, `unsupportedFormat` and `recognizerUnavailable` must XCTFail or XCTSkip with the reason named — never silently pass. This single change converts a test that proves nothing into one that at minimum proves the pipeline reached the recognizer.

TIER 2 — cover the truncation-prone logic without any recognizer (pure unit tests, no TCC, no model).
Nothing downstream of the recognizer is covered today, and it is where the silent-truncation risk lives:
  - `transcribeInSegments` drops a whole segment on empty text with only a warning (AudioTranscriptionService.swift:308-318) and swallows an entire segment's audio on any "no speech" error (319-325). A 90-minute recording with one bad 10-minute block loses that block and reports success. Feed synthetic `TranscriptionResult`s and assert every non-empty segment survives and that the confidence weighting is right.
  - `offsetSegments` (378-387) — assert timestamps offset by exactly startSeconds across the boundary.
  - `analysisToDocument` (SpeechAnalyzerService.swift:272-301) and `transcriptionToDocument` (AudioTranscriptionService.swift:409-424) — assert the header block plus the full body, and that an empty transcript is not dressed up as ~120 characters of metadata and indexed as a success.

TIER 2b — one-line regression pin for the shipped defect:
`XCTAssertTrue(SpeechAnalyzerService.shared.isSpeechAnalyzerAvailable)` under `if #available(iOS 26.0, *)`. Fails today, catches the canImport defect with no audio at all.

TIER 3 — the actual real-speech test.
FIXTURE FORMAT: synthesize at test time, check in no binary. `AVSpeechSynthesizer.writeUtterance(_:toBufferCallback:)` (AVFAudio AVSpeechSynthesis.h:240, iOS 13+) with a pinned voice identifier, pinned rate, and a fixed utterance built from `IngestionFixtureFactory.serviceTable` strings so the existing `rowAssociationProbes` machinery can be reused. Append buffers to an AVAudioFile, 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM.

Six corrections. None unseats the root cause; the first is a real bug in the proposed fix and must be carried forward.

1. TIER 1 AS WRITTEN WOULD REPRODUCE THE DEFECT IT FIXES. At the seam the test observes, `TranscriptionError.authorizationDenied` never appears as itself. DocumentProcessor.swift:8494-8496 catches `TranscriptionError` and rethrows `DocumentProcessingError.audioTranscriptionFailed(error.localizedDescription)`. So `.threw`'s payload for the authorization case is `audioTranscriptionFailed("Speech recognition permission denied. Enable in Settings -> Privacy -> Speech Recognition.")` — the same enum case the plan says to ACCEPT. Discriminating on the case name would pass on the authorization throw and leave the test exactly as vacuous. Tier 1 must match on the message substring: accept `audioTranscriptionEmpty` or a description containing "no speech"; fail or skip on descriptions containing "permission denied", "not available for this language", or "Unsupported audio format". The three TranscriptionError.errorDescription strings at AudioTranscriptionService.swift:52-56 are distinguishable by substring, so this is implementable — just not as specified.

2. TIER 2b ADDS A PERMANENTLY RED TEST. `XCTAssertTrue(SpeechAnalyzerService.shared.isSpeechAnalyzerAvailable)` fails today by design, so it cannot land in a green suite. It needs `XCTExpectFailure` with the reason named, or should be reshaped into an honesty assertion (the availability flag and the engine name in the log/telemetry must agree) so it passes now and fails when they diverge. Also, since the property is a compile-time constant false, the assertion may draw a constant-condition warning. Secondary: SpeechAnalyzerService is `@MainActor`, so any test touching `.shared` needs `@MainActor` or `await`.

3. SCOPE IMPRECISION IN CLAIM (1). "before the URL is validated, before AVURLAsset loads" is true of AudioTranscriptionService.transcribe in isolation, but not of the end-to-end path the test actually runs: SpeechAnalyzerService.analyze already ran `canAnalyze` (:113) and `asset.load(.duration)` (:118-119) before delegating. The existing test therefore does prove the WAV is a parseable container under the 2h cap. That is trivial coverage, and "exercised none of transcription" survives, but the sentence overstates as written.

4. THE TEST ACCEPTS TWO INDISTINGUISHABLE NON-TRANSCRIPTION THROWS, NOT ONE. If TCC somehow reports `.authorized`, the next gate is `SFSpeechRecognizer(locale:)?.isAvailable` at :158-167, throwing `recognizerUnavailable` — also a bare throw the test accepts. This strengthens the diagnosis rather than weakening it, and the fix's skip list already names both, but the write-up presents authorization as the single explanation.

But `simctl privacy <dev> grant all <bundle>` exists and may map to a broader TCC set that includes kTCCServiceSpeechRecognition. I did not test it (it needs a booted simulator). Run that one command before committing to Tier 3's skip-only shape; do not publish "cannot be pre-granted" as established until then.
